tickets.title: Spike: Model Armor screen latency and fail-closed
tickets.summary: Measure Model Armor sanitizeUserPrompt latency and record ADR-009 evidence.
tickets.description: Spike (E4 'Spikes first'). Call Model Armor REST (template = MODEL_ARMOR_TEMPLATE) from a Cloud Run-like environment with 200 redacted prompts of 50-2000 chars (benign, injection, jailbreak). Record p50/p95/p99 latency, false-positive rate on the benign set, detection rate on the injection set, and behaviour at a forced 500 ms timeout. Output: an ADR addendum in context/projects/finadvisor/arch/decisions.md under ADR-009 with the numbers and a keep/change verdict for MODEL_ARMOR_TIMEOUT_MS=500 and fail-closed. Arch: ADR-009 'Model Armor input screen in parallel with embed (500 ms timeout, fail closed)'; 4.5 guardrails. Out of scope: production client (see the Model Armor client ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Given 200 prompts, when the benchmark script runs, then p50, p95, p99 latency and false-positive and detection rates are written to the ADR addendum.
Given the 500 ms timeout is applied client-side, when p99 is above 500 ms, then the ADR states the resulting fail-closed rate as a percentage and a decision (keep or change).
The benchmark script is committed and re-runnable with one command and exits non-zero if the template is unreachable.

tickets.title: Spike: Presidio latency and recall on synthetic corpus
tickets.summary: Measure Presidio en_core_web_sm latency and PII recall on the synthetic corpus.
tickets.description: Spike. No official figure exists (ADR-009). With presidio-analyzer 2.2.x and spaCy en_core_web_sm (PRESIDIO_SPACY_MODEL), run on (a) 500 synthetic advisor questions with injected PII (names, emails, phones, account numbers, national ids, addresses) and (b) 1000-char and 4000-char inputs. Record warm per-call p50/p95, cold-start time, memory, and per-entity recall and precision. Test pseudonymization round-trip (placeholders stable within a turn). Record as an ADR-009 addendum; propose INPUT_MAX_CHARS and the entity list/score threshold. Out of scope: wiring into chat.
acceptance_criteria: Given the 500-question set, when the benchmark runs, then per-entity recall and precision and latency p50/p95 are recorded in the ADR addendum.
If overall recall on injected PII is below 0.90 the ADR lists the missed entity classes and a mitigation (custom recognizer or lower threshold); the verdict is stated either way.
The proposed INPUT_MAX_CHARS is justified by the 4000-char latency measurement.

tickets.title: Spike: Sonnet 5.5 prompt-cache hit behaviour with versioned tools
tickets.summary: Measure prompt-cache hits for system prompt plus tools on claude-sonnet-5-5.
tickets.description: Spike. Using the Anthropic SDK against claude-sonnet-5-5 (cache minimum 512 tokens per ADR-006), put cache_control on the end of tools+system and send 20 sequential and 20 concurrent requests with varying tenant/user/date text after the breakpoint. Record cache_read_input_tokens vs cache_creation_input_tokens, hit rate, TTFT with and without hit, and show that changing one tool definition invalidates the cache. Repeat once for claude-sonnet-4-6 (1,024-token minimum) to feed the fallback. Record as an ADR-006 addendum. Out of scope: the production LLMClient.
acceptance_criteria: Given 20 sequential requests with a stable prefix, when run, then the hit rate and cache_read tokens are recorded and the ADR states whether the prefix reaches the 512-token minimum.
Given one tool definition is edited, when the next request is sent, then cache_read_input_tokens is 0 and cache_creation is >0; the result is recorded.
TTFT p50 with hit and without hit are both recorded.

tickets.title: Add E4 settings keys and the stable error-code mapping
tickets.summary: Typed Settings for E4 keys and a single error-code to HTTP/SSE mapping with fixed messages.
tickets.description: Add to the pydantic-settings Settings class (6.6), no secret default, missing required key fails boot: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL_ANSWER, LLM_MODEL_AUX, LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK, LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED(false), LLM_MAX_ITERATIONS(3), LLM_MAX_TOKENS, LLM_TIMEOUT_S, LLM_RETRIES, LLM_BREAKER_*, PROMPT_VERSION, INPUT_MAX_CHARS, MODEL_ARMOR_TEMPLATE, MODEL_ARMOR_TIMEOUT_MS(500), MODEL_ARMOR_FAIL_OPEN(false), PRESIDIO_SPACY_MODEL, TENANT_TOKEN_BUDGET, TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY, SSE_HEARTBEAT_S, SSE_REPLAY_TTL_S, TURN_LEASE_S, HISTORY_MAX_TURNS(6), HISTORY_MAX_TOKENS(3000), EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE. Values marked 'set in E4' come from the spikes and are documented in .env.example. Implement guardrails error mapping (6.1): UNAUTHENTICATED 401, FORBIDDEN 403, INPUT_TOO_LONG 413, INPUT_BLOCKED, GUARD_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED 429 with Retry-After, TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, LLM_UNAVAILABLE, RETRIEVAL_UNAVAILABLE, TURN_INTERRUPTED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED 409, INTERNAL. HTTP error body is {"error":{"code","message","request_id","retryable"}} with a fixed message per code, never exception text. Replaces the MVP src/errors.py behaviour that leaks exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: Given a missing required key, when Settings loads, then boot raises (unit test per key group).

Given each exception class raised in a handler, when mapped, then the response body has the stable code and the fixed message and contains no substring of the exception text (parametrized test over every code).
X-Request-Id from Kong is echoed in error.request_id (test).

tickets.title: LLMClient: streaming, timeouts, jittered retries, config-only models
tickets.summary: In-process LLMClient over the Anthropic SDK with streaming, timeouts and retries.
tickets.description: Implement src/llm (ADR-005). stream(messages, tools, system, model=None) yields normalized events (text delta, tool_use, usage, stop_reason). Explicit connect/read timeouts from LLM_TIMEOUT_S; retries LLM_RETRIES with exponential backoff and full jitter on 429/5xx/overloaded/connection errors only (never on 4xx other than 429); max_tokens=LLM_MAX_TOKENS always set; model ids only from Settings; base URL from ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. The request builder must never send temperature, top_p or top_k (removed 2026-10-21, 400). Replaces LiteLLM use in the MVP (litellm/ dir out of scope to delete unless E1 owns it). Out of scope: breaker, fallback, caching.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stubbed 529 twice then 200, when streaming, then exactly 3 attempts are made with sleeps drawn from the jitter range (seeded test).
Given a 400 response, when streaming, then no retry occurs and LLM_UNAVAILABLE-mappable error is raised.
Given any request, when captured at the HTTP layer, then the body has no temperature, top_p or top_k keys and has max_tokens (test).
Given no hardcoded model string in src/llm, a grep-based test fails if a literal 'claude-' id appears outside config/tests.

tickets.title: LLMClient: circuit breaker and eval-gated same-provider fallback
tickets.summary: Add a circuit breaker and a fallback to LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK only when LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED is true.
tickets.description: Extend LLMClient. Breaker params from LLM_BREAKER_* (failure threshold, window, open duration, half-open probes); when open, calls fail fast with LLM_UNAVAILABLE. Fallback: after primary exhausts retries or the breaker is open, if and only if LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED is true, retry once on LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK (claude-sonnet-4-6; same provider only, never another vendor); the usage record carries the model actually used. Fallback has its own prompt cache and 1,024-token minimum (use spike result). Config default false until the eval gate passes (E7). Quote ADR-005: 'same-provider fallback only ... enabled only if it passes the eval gate'.
acceptance_criteria: Given primary forced to fail and LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=false, when streaming, then LLM_UNAVAILABLE is raised and the fallback model is never called (test).
Given primary forced to fail and LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true, when streaming, then the fallback model is used and usage.model equals LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK; no temperature/top_p/top_k sent.
Given N consecutive failures, when the breaker opens, then the next call fails without a network request until the open duration passes (fake clock test); half-open success closes it.

tickets.title: LLMClient: prompt caching, versioned tools, model retirement check
tickets.summary: Cache system prompt plus tools, version them with PROMPT_VERSION and fail readiness on retired models.
tickets.description: Place cache_control at the end of tools then system (cache order tools, system, messages); tenant/user/date text only in messages after the breakpoint. Tool definitions and system prompt are built by one function keyed on PROMPT_VERSION; a test hashes them so a change without a PROMPT_VERSION bump fails CI. Apply the spike (E4-T3) result: if the prefix is under the model minimum, log a warning with token count. Add a retirement table (model id -> retirement date) in config and a check used by /readyz (model availability item, 6.1) and a CI test that fails when a configured model is retired or retires within 30 days. Record cache_read/creation tokens in usage. Quote ADR-006: 'tool definitions are versioned with the prompt because changing them invalidates the cache'.
acceptance_criteria: Given two consecutive requests with the same prefix against the stub, when built, then the system/tools blocks are byte-identical and carry cache_control; tenant/user/date text appears only after the breakpoint (test).
Given a tool schema edited without a PROMPT_VERSION bump, when CI runs, then the hash test fails.
Given LLM_MODEL_ANSWER set to a retired id, when /readyz is called, then it reports not ready; and the CI retirement test fails for a model retiring within 30 days.
Usage events include cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens.

tickets.title: Guard-in: input cap and Presidio pseudonymization
tickets.summary: Cap input length and pseudonymize PII before embed, LLM, traces and logs.
tickets.description: In src/guardrails: reject over INPUT_MAX_CHARS with INPUT_TOO_LONG (413) before any other work; Presidio AnalyzerEngine (spaCy PRESIDIO_SPACY_MODEL=en_core_web_sm, loaded once per process at startup, entity list/threshold from spike E4-T2) returns the redacted text plus a placeholder map held only in request memory. The redacted text is the only text passed to embedding, Model Armor, LLM, Langfuse, OTel attributes and logs. Replace the MVP src/pii fallback. Quote ADR-009: 'Presidio in-process pseudonymization ... before embed / LLM / traces / logs'. Out of scope: output redaction.
acceptance_criteria: Given a question containing an email, a phone number and a person name, when guard-in runs, then the returned text has none of them and contains typed placeholders (unit test).
Given input of INPUT_MAX_CHARS+1, when guard-in runs, then INPUT_TOO_LONG is raised before the Presidio engine is invoked (mock call count 0).
Given the benchmark corpus from E4-T2, recall is at least the value recorded in the ADR (regression test with threshold).
Warm p95 latency on a 1000-char input stays within the ADR-recorded bound (marked perf test).

tickets.title: Model Armor input screen client, fail closed
tickets.summary: Screen redacted input via Model Armor with a 500 ms timeout that fails closed.
tickets.description: Client in src/guardrails calling Model Armor sanitizeUserPrompt with MODEL_ARMOR_TEMPLATE on the redacted text; timeout MODEL_ARMOR_TIMEOUT_MS (500). Verdict match -> INPUT_BLOCKED (not an LLM call, SSE error or HTTP per 6.1). Timeout, 5xx or auth error -> GUARD_UNAVAILABLE and the turn stops, unless MODEL_ARMOR_FAIL_OPEN is true (default false; boot warns in prod profile if true). The screen runs concurrently (asyncio.gather) with the Voyage embed; if the screen blocks or fails, the embed result is discarded and no retrieval SQL runs. The REST API only detects; the app acts (ADR-009). Use verdict/latency findings from E4-T1.
acceptance_criteria: Given Model Armor stubbed to delay 600 ms, when screened, then GUARD_UNAVAILABLE is returned at about 500 ms and no retrieval call is made (test with timing assertion <700 ms).
Given a blocked verdict, when screened, then INPUT_BLOCKED is raised and neither Anthropic nor DB retrieval is called.
Given the embed and screen stubs each sleeping 300 ms, when run together, then total wall time is under 450 ms (concurrency test).
Given MODEL_ARMOR_FAIL_OPEN=false and a 5xx, the result is GUARD_UNAVAILABLE (never pass-through).

tickets.title: Tool dispatcher: JSON tool_result, validation, max iterations
tickets.summary: Dispatch the four tools with Pydantic validation, JSON-encoded results and no exception text.
tickets.description: In src/agent/tools, per 6.3: unknown tool names rejected; arguments validated by Pydantic models (search_firm_kb top_k bounded; lookup_product_factsheet product_name; lookup_suitability_rule product_category and enum client_risk_profile); no tool accepts tenant, tier, jurisdiction or licenses (tests assert the schemas lack those fields); output is model_dump_json(); failures return {"error_code": ...} with no exception text; iterations capped at LLM_MAX_ITERATIONS (3). Retrieved text only ever appears in a tool_result block, never in system. Tools call the E3 services (search_firm_kb, factsheet, suitability) through RetrievalService(principal); this ticket does not reimplement them. Tool definitions registered for the prompt-cache builder (E4-T7).
acceptance_criteria: Given a tool call with an unknown name, when dispatched, then the result is {"error_code":"UNKNOWN_TOOL"} and no service is called.
Given a tool raising ValueError('secret sql'), when dispatched, then the tool_result JSON contains error_code and the string 'secret sql' appears nowhere in it (test).
Given every tool's JSON schema, when inspected, then no property named tenant_id, tier, jurisdiction or licenses exists.
Given a model that requests tools 4 times, when the loop runs, then it stops after 3 iterations.

tickets.title: CitationVerifier implementation and server citation events
tickets.summary: Deterministic verifier: every [n] in retrieved chunk ids with quote overlap; server emits citation events.
tickets.description: Implement the CitationVerifier Protocol defined in E3 (the cache hit path in E3-T14 already depends on it). Rules (ADR-009, 8.1 LLM05): every [n] in the answer maps to a retrieved chunk of this turn (id set from the retrieval result); a cited claim must overlap the chunk text by a deterministic quote/token-overlap threshold (threshold a config value tuned in evals, default documented). On accept, build the SSE 'citation' event {index, chunk_id, source_title, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, stale, excerpt}; excerpt passes through the output redactor (G-16); stale is computed server-side. The model never emits citation events itself. Verifier failure behaviour: drop the uncited sentence marker and set finish_reason accordingly or return refusal; choose per arch (see questions). Uses retrieval.fetch_chunks(ids) for chunk data.
acceptance_criteria: Given an answer citing [4] when retrieved ids map only to 1..3, when verified, then it is rejected and no citation event is emitted (verifier test).
Given an answer whose [n] set is a subset of retrieved chunks and with quote overlap above threshold, when verified, then one citation event per distinct n is returned with a redacted excerpt.
Given a chunk excerpt containing an email, when the event is built, then the excerpt contains no email (test).
Property test: for random answers, every [n] present in emitted citation events is in the retrieved chunk-id set.

tickets.title: Sentence-buffered output PII redaction
tickets.summary: Buffer streamed text to sentence boundaries and redact PII before emitting delta events.
tickets.description: In src/guardrails: wrap the LLM text stream; accumulate until a sentence boundary (or max buffer length to bound latency, config), run Presidio on the sentence (and restore pseudonym placeholders only if arch allows; default: leave redacted), then emit. Flush remaining buffer at end of stream. Must handle [n] markers split across chunks without breaking them. Quote ADR-009: 'sentence-buffered output PII redaction ... adds a small latency to first visible tokens'. Record the added first-delta latency in the PR.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stream chunked mid-sentence containing an email split across two chunks, when redacted, then no emitted delta contains the email in full or in part (test).
Given a stream ending without a final period, when finished, then the remaining text is flushed (test).
Given the marker '[1' and '2]' split across chunks, when processed, then the emitted text contains '[12]' unchanged or '[1]' per original (no corruption; parametrized test).
Added latency before first delta is measured on a stub and reported; test fails if the buffer exceeds the configured max.

tickets.title: turn_events store and SSE v2 event encoding
tickets.summary: Persist ordered events per turn and encode them as SSE with ids and a client-safe schema.
tickets.description: Define event models (6.2): turn, meta, tool, delta, citation, refusal, error, done with exact data shapes; encode as 'id: <seq>\nevent: <name>\ndata: <json>'. Implement an EventSink that assigns strictly increasing seq per turn (turn at seq 0), inserts into turn_events (table from E1 schema; if absent see questions) in short transactions, batching delta events (documented interval) so the DB is not hit per token, and sends heartbeat comment lines every SSE_HEARTBEAT_S. Client-visible events are built only from these models: tool events carry tool name, status, tool_use_id; no payloads, inputs or exception text (G-04); error events carry {code, retryable} only. Do not make DB calls while holding a stream open longer than a short tx.
acceptance_criteria: Given events of every type are emitted in a test turn, when serialized, then none contains tool input/output payloads or exception text (test over all event types with a poisoned tool result and exception).
Given a turn, when events are persisted, then seq is 0,1,2,... strictly increasing with no gaps and turn is seq 0.
Given SSE_HEARTBEAT_S=1 and no events for 3 s, when streaming, then at least 2 comment lines ': hb' are sent.
Delta batching: 1000 token deltas produce fewer than 1000 inserts (assert insert count).

tickets.title: POST /v1/chat with Idempotency-Key and replay
tickets.summary: Idempotent chat endpoint: same key and body replays, different body returns 409.
tickets.description: POST /v1/chat requires header Idempotency-Key and body {conversation_id?, message}. turn_id derived from the Idempotency-Key (deterministic, per principal/tenant namespace). Short tx: insert turn_events seq 0 ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING plus store a request-body hash with the turn; if the row existed with the same hash, stream a replay of persisted events (then tail until done) instead of generating; a different hash returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Missing header -> 400 with a stable code. Auth and principal first. Streams text/event-stream; Kong passes it unbuffered. Orchestrator call is a stub interface here (implemented in the orchestrator tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Given the same Idempotency-Key and body sent twice, when the second arrives, then the LLM stub is called once and the second response replays identical events (test counting stub calls).
Given the same key with a different body, when posted, then status is 409 with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
Given two concurrent requests with the same key, when both arrive, then exactly one generation runs (race test).
Given a different tenant using the same key string, when posted, then it is a distinct turn (no cross-tenant replay).

tickets.title: GET /v1/chat/{turn_id}/events resume and TURN_INTERRUPTED
tickets.summary: Resume a dropped stream from Last-Event-ID, tail to done, and detect dead producers.
tickets.description: Endpoint (6.1/6.2): owner of the turn only (403/404 otherwise, RLS-scoped); header Last-Event-ID; replay turn_events with seq > Last-Event-ID, then tail (poll or LISTEN, documented) until done; heartbeat as in E4-T13. If the last persisted event is older than TURN_LEASE_S and no done/error exists, append once error {code: TURN_INTERRUPTED, retryable: true} and end; the append must be idempotent across concurrent resumers. Events older than SSE_REPLAY_TTL_S are no longer replayable (410 or documented code).
acceptance_criteria: Given a turn of 20 events and a client that disconnects after seq 7, when it reconnects with Last-Event-ID 7, then it receives exactly seq 8..N with no duplicates or gaps (test).
Given the producer stops and TURN_LEASE_S passes, when two resumers connect concurrently, then exactly one TURN_INTERRUPTED error row exists in turn_events.
Given another advisor's turn_id, when requested, then no events are returned (403/404 test).
Given Last-Event-ID absent, the stream starts from seq 0.

tickets.title: Conversations and messages persistence with history window
tickets.summary: Persist conversations/messages and load the last 6 turns within 3k tokens.
tickets.description: Repository in src/agent (using E1 tables conversations and messages, monthly range partitions, columns incl. retrieval_degraded and citations (redacted)). Functions: create/get conversation (owner = principal), insert user message (redacted text only) and assistant message, load history = last HISTORY_MAX_TURNS turns trimmed to HISTORY_MAX_TOKENS (token count method documented), soft delete via DELETE /v1/conversations/{id} (204), GET /v1/conversations and /messages with cursor. All in short, tenant-scoped transactions. Stored text is the redacted text.
acceptance_criteria: Given 10 prior turns, when history loads, then at most 6 turns are returned and total tokens <= 3000 (test with a long-turn fixture).
Given another advisor's conversation id, when GET messages, then 404/403 (RLS test).
Given DELETE then GET, the conversation is excluded and returns 204 once.
Given a user message containing PII, the stored content equals the redacted text (test).

tickets.title: Follow-up condensation with Haiku
tickets.summary: Rewrite a follow-up into a standalone query only when history exists.
tickets.description: When history is non-empty, call LLMClient with LLM_MODEL_AUX (claude-haiku-5-5), small max_tokens, input = redacted history + redacted question, output = standalone redacted question used for embed/retrieval/cache key. No history -> no call. Failure or timeout falls back to the original question (not an error). Output re-passes the guard-in redactor. No temperature/top_p/top_k.
acceptance_criteria: Given empty history, when preparing a turn, then the aux LLM stub is called 0 times.
Given history and the stub returning a rewritten query, when prepared, then retrieval receives the rewritten query.
Given the aux call timing out, when prepared, then the original question is used and the turn continues.
Given a rewritten query containing an email, then it is redacted before use (test).

tickets.title: Orchestrator pre-LLM stages: cache, screen+embed, retrieval, gate
tickets.summary: Retrieve-first pipeline up to the gate, with the meta event and refusal path.
tickets.description: src/agent orchestrator order (4.5, Flow 1): guard-in (cap, Presidio) -> condensation (if history) -> answer_cache lookup (E3-T13/T14 store, key from the normalized redacted question; hit re-fetches via fetch_chunks, re-runs the CitationVerifier, a miss on invisible chunk) -> on miss: Model Armor screen in parallel with Voyage embed -> RetrievalService search+rerank+gate (E3) in short transactions -> emit 'meta' {retrieval_degraded, reason?} once after rerank and store messages.retrieval_degraded. Gate failure emits 'refusal' {NO_FIRM_DOCUMENTATION, escalate_offer} then done(finish_reason gate) with no LLM call. Cache hit path emits delta/citation events from the verified cached answer and skips screen and embed. Failures map to one error event with a code (RETRIEVAL_UNAVAILABLE etc). Cache write after a verified, non-escalating turn is in the next ticket's persist step.
acceptance_criteria: Given the gate stub failing, when a turn runs, then events are turn, meta, refusal, done(gate) and the LLM stub is called 0 times.
Given the reranker stub returning 429, when run, then meta.retrieval_degraded is true with reason rerank_429 and the stored messages.retrieval_degraded is true (equality test across both).
Given a cache hit, when run, then Model Armor and Voyage stubs are called 0 times and chunks are fetched via fetch_chunks.
Given a cache hit citing a chunk no longer visible to the principal, then it behaves as a miss.
Given Model Armor timeout, the turn ends with error GUARD_UNAVAILABLE and no retrieval SQL.

tickets.title: Orchestrator LLM loop: streaming with tools, verifier and redaction
tickets.summary: One streaming LLM call with tools, max 3 iterations, wired to verifier and output redaction.
tickets.description: After the gate passes (parent expansion and staleness via E3), inject retrieval as a JSON-encoded tool_result for a synthetic search_firm_kb tool_use, then stream via LLMClient with tools (4 tools, E4-T10 dispatcher), prompt cache (E4-T7) and the versioned system prompt (update MVP src/agent/system_prompt.py: no secrets or tenant data, 'today' and tenant/user text after the cache breakpoint, instruct citing with [n]). Emit 'tool' events (name/status/tool_use_id) on tool_use start and result; text goes through sentence-buffered redaction to 'delta'; when the answer completes (or per sentence), the CitationVerifier runs and citation events are emitted; verifier rejection handled per questions. Max LLM_MAX_ITERATIONS. finish_reason in (end_turn, max_tokens, refusal, gate). LLM failures after breaker/fallback -> error LLM_UNAVAILABLE.
acceptance_criteria: Given the LLM stub citing [n] not in retrieved ids, when the turn runs, then no citation event for that n is emitted and the verifier outcome is recorded (end-to-end verifier test).
Given a tool raising an exception with sensitive text, then no emitted event or tool_result contains that text.
Given the LLM stub requesting tools forever, then the loop stops at 3 iterations and done is emitted.
Given the retrieved text contains 'ignore previous instructions', it appears only inside a tool_result block in the captured Anthropic request, never in system (test).
Delta events contain no PII injected in the stubbed answer.

tickets.title: escalate_to_compliance persistence and GET /v1/escalations
tickets.summary: Persist escalations with server-side licenses and an outbox event; list endpoint.
tickets.description: Tool (6.3): input {reason, product_class}; licenses read from Principal/advisors.licenses (never tool args); insert into escalations (E1 table) and an outbox row in one transaction; returns {escalation_id, status:'pending_review'}; client sees tool name+status only (G-18). A turn that calls it is flagged side_effect so it is never written to answer_cache. GET /v1/escalations: compliance_officer sees tenant escalations, others only their own (RLS + role check). Reason text is redacted before persist.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tool call, when executed, then exactly one escalations row and one outbox row exist, in the same transaction (rollback test: failure of the outbox insert leaves no escalation).
Given an advisor with licenses X, the stored license snapshot equals advisors.licenses and any 'licenses' argument from the model is rejected by schema validation.
Given a non-officer, GET /v1/escalations returns only own rows; officer returns tenant rows; other tenant rows never appear.
Given a turn that escalated, the answer cache write is skipped (test).

tickets.title: Outbox writer and turn persist transaction
tickets.summary: Write chat.audit, chat.usage and sampled eval.sample outbox rows in the turn-persist transaction.
tickets.description: Module events (4.5): insert-only outbox writer taking the current transaction; no Kafka client or credentials in chat-api (import-linter contract + test). Turn persist = one short transaction: assistant message (retrieval_degraded, finish_reason, redacted citations), final turn_events flush, outbox rows chat.audit and chat.usage (tokens in/out, cache tokens, model used, latency, tenant) and, with probability EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE on completed turns, eval.sample.v1; answer_cache write (E3 store) when eligible (no side-effect tool, verifier passed). Payloads use redacted text only. Event schema names/versions follow the 6.4 topic catalogue (verify against it).
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed turn, when persisted, then one chat.audit and one chat.usage outbox row exist in the same transaction as the assistant message (kill-after-message test: no orphan rows).
Given EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0 an eval.sample row is written; at 0.0 none (seeded-RNG test).
Given chat-api code, importing a kafka client fails the import-linter contract.
Given PII in the stubbed answer, outbox payloads contain only redacted text (test).

tickets.title: Per-tenant token budget and concurrency limits
tickets.summary: Enforce TENANT_TOKEN_BUDGET and TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY before generation.
tickets.description: Before the LLM call, check the tenant's token usage against TENANT_TOKEN_BUDGET (window defined in questions; source: usage rows already written, no new infra unless arch lists one) and in-flight turns against TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY. Exceeded budget -> TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED; concurrency -> RATE_LIMITED 429 with Retry-After. Concurrency slot released in finally. Both limits are per tenant, not per instance (state in Postgres or Valkey per questions).
acceptance_criteria: Given budget exhausted, when a turn starts, then error TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED is returned and the LLM stub is called 0 times.
Given TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 and 3 simultaneous turns, then the third gets 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; after one finishes a new turn is accepted.
Given a turn that raises, the concurrency slot is released (test).

tickets.title: Admin: PATCH /v1/admin/advisors/{id}
tickets.summary: Tenant admins update advisors directly, bumping entitlement_version with an outbox event.
tickets.description: Endpoint (6.1): role tenant_admin via principal; body {role?, tier?, jurisdictions?, licenses?, status?} validated; direct UPDATE advisors (policy allows tenant_admin only), bump entitlement_version, outbox AdvisorEntitlementChanged in the same transaction; own-tenant only (RLS). Takes effect within ENTITLEMENT_CACHE_TTL_S (no Kafka invalidation).
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant_admin, when patching tier, then 200, entitlement_version increments by 1 and one outbox row exists.
Given a non-admin, then 403 FORBIDDEN and no row changes.
Given an advisor of another tenant, then 404 and no change (RLS test).
Given an invalid tier value, 422/400 with a stable code.

tickets.title: Admin: ACL change and delete requests with status endpoint
tickets.summary: ACL change/delete returns 202 and writes one acl_change_requests row plus one outbox row.
tickets.description: Endpoints (6.1, ADR-022): POST /v1/admin/documents/{id}/acl-changes {tier_required?, jurisdiction?} and DELETE /v1/admin/documents/{id} (action=delete), role tenant_admin; in one transaction insert acl_change_requests (pending) and outbox AclChangeRequested (acl.changes.v1) and return 202 {request_id}; validate that the document is visible to the admin's tenant by reading via RetrievalService (no write to content tables). GET /v1/admin/acl-changes/{request_id} returns {status: pending|applied|failed, applied_at}. Given a non-admin, 403 and zero rows.
Given the fa_app role, a privilege test asserts no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grant on documents, chunks and suitability_rules (information_schema.role_table_grants query).
Given a request id of another tenant, GET status returns 404.

tickets.title: Leak-path tests: PII never reaches Voyage, Anthropic, logs or Langfuse
tickets.summary: End-to-end test that injected PII is absent from every outbound call, log line and trace.
tickets.description: Integration test: run the full orchestrator with stubs capturing (a) Voyage embed and rerank request bodies, (b) Anthropic requests incl. aux condensation, (c) Model Armor request, (d) captured log records and OTel/Langfuse span attributes, (e) outbox payloads and turn_events. Inject PII (email, phone, name, account number) in the question and in history. Assert none of the raw values appear anywhere; also assert client SSE events contain no tool payloads or exception text across all event types. Ensure Langfuse masking is wired if LANGFUSE_ENABLED (mask before export).
acceptance_criteria: Given PII in the question, when a turn runs, then a scan of all captured outbound bodies, logs, spans and outbox rows finds zero occurrences of the raw values (test fails if one leaks).
Given a poisoned tool exception text, the full SSE capture contains no part of it.
Given LANGFUSE_ENABLED=true with a capture exporter, span attributes contain redacted text only.

tickets.title: Resume, idempotency and failure end-to-end tests
tickets.summary: Integration tests for dropped connections, key reuse, fallback gating and meta consistency.
tickets.description: Add the epic's integration tests against a real Postgres: (1) drop the connection mid-stream, resume with Last-Event-ID, final event list equals an uninterrupted run; (2) same Idempotency-Key twice -> one LLM call; different body -> 409; (3) meta.retrieval_degraded equals messages.retrieval_degraded for degraded and non-degraded turns; (4) with primary forced to fail, fallback used only when LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED is true; (5) Model Armor 500 ms timeout -> GUARD_UNAVAILABLE; (6) every emitted [n] is within retrieved chunk ids. Wire into CI.
acceptance_criteria: Test (1) fails if any event is missing or duplicated after resume.
Test (2) fails if the LLM stub call count is not 1, or the status is not 409 on a different body.
Test (3) fails if the two flags differ for either case.
Tests (4)-(6) fail as described in their assertions and run in CI on every PR.

tickets.title: TTFT benchmark on 10k-chunk corpus with a real LLM
tickets.summary: Measure TTFT p50/p95 against the overview 2.1 target and fail if above.
tickets.description: Script and CI-manual job: load the 10k-chunk synthetic corpus (E3-T16 fixture), real Voyage and Anthropic (claude-sonnet-5-5), Model Armor and Presidio on, prompt cache warm; run at least 200 turns including 30% follow-ups and a cache-hit mix reported separately. TTFT = request received to first delta event. Report p50/p95, stage breakdown (guard, embed/screen, retrieval, rerank, LLM first token). Targets from overview 2.1: p50 < 2.0 s, p95 < 3.5 s; script exits non-zero above them. Save results in the repo docs and an ADR note.
acceptance_criteria: Given the 10k corpus and real LLM, when the benchmark runs 200 turns, then p50 < 2.0 s and p95 < 3.5 s or the command exits non-zero.
The report lists per-stage p50/p95 so a regression is attributable.
Cache-hit and cache-miss turns are reported as separate distributions.
